references.text: This text in Leviticus contains the parallel law regarding unclean flying creeping things and gives more detailed instructions on which winged insects are permitted and not permitted to eat.
Here the prohibition against eating creeping things, including those that crawl on the ground, is expanded, emphasizing that all such creatures are detestable.
This text provides the theological basis for avoiding unclean animals - the people of Israel shall be holy because the Lord is holy.
The general principle that the Israelites must not eat anything detestable, which introduces the entire section on clean and unclean animals in Deuteronomy.
